 HuffPost Staff — HuffPost Leave a Comment 3 minutes ago Ben Blanchet Taylor Hill via Getty Images Beyoncé's Latest Grammys Achievement Is Unprecedented
 Beyoncé became the first artist with 100 nominations in Grammy Awards history on Monday, roughly two years after she passed her husband Jay-Z as the most-nominated artist.
 The singer — who already has a record 35 Grammy Awards, the most of any artist in history — captured her 100th nomination for her song “Morning Dew (Donk)” in the Best R&B Solo Performance category.
 Queen Bey surprise-dropped the song on the Fourth of July as part of the 20th anniversary edition of her 2006 album “B’Day.”
 Watch the full nominations announcement livestream here and find out if Beyoncé takes another gramophone at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards on Feb. 7.

 23 minutes ago Marita Vlachou Willie Geist To Exit MS NOW
 Will Geist, the longtime co-host of “Morning Joe,” announced he is leaving MS NOW next month.
 “It is with a very heavy heart, heavy with memories and experiences and friends and family, like the two people on the screen with me right now that I announce my run on ‘Morning Joe’ will end next month,” he said, speaking alongside Mika Brzezinski and Joe Scarborough.
 Geist will expand his role at NBC News and “Today” following his MS NOW exit.
 “Over the past 10 years, Willie has transformed Sunday ‘Today’ from a broadcast into a distinctive, multi platform brand with a voice and identity all its own,” Libby Leist, executive VP of “Today” and lifestyle at NBC, said in a statement. “We’re thrilled he’ll now be able to focus full-time on building the brand in new ways and bringing his exceptional journalism to all of our platforms.”

 50 minutes ago Risk Of Nuclear Accident In Ukraine Increasing This Winter, Atomic Safety Regulators Say
 The risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is increasing this winter, nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries said on Monday, urging Russia to stop its attacks on the country’s power infrastructure.
 Moscow has stepped up its drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian energy installations, such as plants, power lines and electricity substations, a system already weakened after nearly five years of conflict.
 “Together we... express our deep concern about the increasing risks to nuclear safety arising from Russia’s war against Ukraine, and its continued attacks on the country’s energy infrastructure,” the bodies said in a joint statement seen by Reuters ahead of publication.

 1 hr 40 mins ago Marita Vlachou FAA, DOT Staff To Brief Congress Following Nationwide Ground Stop
 Staffers from the Federal Aviation Administration and the Department of Transportation will brief Congress on Monday, just days after a nationwide ground stoppage wreaked havoc for travelers across the country.
 Reps. Rick Larsen (D-Wash.), the ranking member on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and André Carson, the ranking member of the subcommittee on aviation, said “FAA and DOT staff will brief our staff on Monday about the additional $30 billion originally requested by the administration.”
 “We also expect to receive clear answers from FAA Administrator Bedford at our early December hearing—unless that can happen sooner,” they added.
 This comes as flight disruptions have eased significantly following Friday’s ground stop.

 1 hr 57 mins ago In Conversation With Peggy Flanagan, The First Native Woman Elected To The Senate
 More than 2,000 people have served as U.S. senators since the country’s founding. Just 65 have been women.
 None has been a Native American woman. Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan (D-Minn.) is about to change that.
 After a resounding midterm victory, Flanagan, an Ojibwe citizen of the White Earth Nation, is headed to Washington, D.C., as a historic first and one of eight new Democrats who won on Nov. 3 and helped flip Senate control to their party. If Mary Peltola wins her race in Alaska, she’ll be the Senate’s ninth new Democrat and its second Indigenous woman.
 HuffPost recently caught up with Flanagan to talk about her historic win, how she feels people underestimated her Senate bid “every step of the way,” her plan to “avenge Minnesota” for ICE’s assault on residents, and why she thinks it’s time for Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) to step aside and let someone new guide the party forward.

 2 hrs 21 mins ago Marita Vlachou via Associated Press Army Soldier Who Survived Deadly Iranian Strike Files Whistleblower Complaint To Congress
 Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom, who survived a deadly Iranian strike on a makeshift U.S. operations center in Kuwait in March, has filed a whistleblower complaint to the House and Senate Armed Services committees, accusing Pentagon leaders of not doing enough to protect troops there, CBS News and CNN reported.
 In an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes,” Ramsbottom, who was injured in the strike, said “there was nothing there designed to protect from an aerial attack,” despite concerns raised about the potential vulnerability.
 “I feel this is a tactical failure by the Army, our leadership, and myself — all the way down to my level,” Ramsbottom told 60 Minutes’ Norah O’Donnell. “We just did not plan this well, and this needs to be a lesson that we learn.”

 3 hrs 15 mins ago Russia Says Its Air Defenses Intercept Over 1,300 Ukrainian Drones In Massive Aerial Attack
 Russian air defenses intercepted 1,336 drones launched by Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Monday, in what appeared to be Kyiv’s biggest aerial attack since Moscow’s all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago.
 Ukraine has scaled up its long-range aerial assaults on Russia, as well as illegally annexed Crimea, the Black and the Azov seas, with more than 1,000 drones used in some attacks in recent months.
 Russia, meanwhile, has battered Ukrainian civilian areas with relentless attacks that seek to make daily life impossible and break morale, especially through strikes on the power grid.

 3 hrs 25 mins ago AAA Forecasts Another Busy — But Not Quite As Busy — Thanksgiving Travel Week
 Pricey plane tickets and expensive gasoline are expected to keep some Americans from traveling this Thanksgiving, but not enough to make much difference in airport security lines and highway traffic, AAA said Monday.
 The auto club federation predicted that 81.5 million people would travel at least 50 miles (80 kilometers) from home between the Tuesday before Thanksgiving and the Monday after the holiday.
 That’s about 121,000 fewer than traveled domestically over Thanksgiving last year, or a one-tenth of a percent decline, AAA said in its annual forecast. If proven accurate, the small drop would end three years of record-setting Thanksgiving travel that followed the COVID-19 pandemic, according to AAA’s calculations.

 Nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards are set to be announced on Monday morning.
 You can watch the presentation starting at 7:45 a.m. ET here .

 3 hrs 46 mins ago Marita Vlachou Trump Admin To Designate Nvidia AI 'National Champion' Despite Huang Scandal: WSJ
 The Trump administration is planning to designate Nvidia as an AI “national champion,” according to The Wall Street Journal , despite the recent scandal involving the company and its former CEO, Jensen Huang.
 The “national champion” initiative spearheaded by the Department of Commerce is meant to make U.S. AI companies more competitive internationally, The Journal reported.
 Other companies expected to get the designation are OpenAI, Microsoft, Amazon and Anthropic, the report said.
 The news comes as Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO following reports of his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

 3 hrs 47 mins ago Trump Heads To Asia Following GOP Midterm Losses
 President Donald Trump heads to Asia this week, hoping to make some big attention-grabbing moves on the world stage after his party suffered deep losses in the midterm elections, diminishing his standing at home.
 The Republican president is using the international trip to try to shift momentum, and he is poised to make a splash with a historic three-way meeting with Presidents Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir Putin of Russia to talk about their nuclear stockpiles. Trump has long boasted about leveraging his relationships with the leaders of two of America’s biggest global adversaries, though he has failed so far to achieve major breakthroughs with them.
